nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number and let $n_0, \dots, n_{r-1}$ be natural numbers with $n = n_0 + \dots + n_{r-1} > 0$. Order the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$ as the natural numbers and order words over it lexicographically. Then the number of Lyndon words over this alphabet in which each letter $i$ occurs exactly $n_i$ times equals, as a rational number, Witt's multigraded value…
nodes.title: Witt's formula for the number of Lyndon words of given content

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number, let $n_0, \dots, n_{r-1}$ be natural numbers, and let $n = n_0 + \dots + n_{r-1}$. The number of words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$ in which each letter $i$ occurs exactly $n_i$ times is the multinomial coefficient $\binom{n}{n_0, \ldots, n_{r-1}} = \frac{n!}{n_0! \cdots n_{r-1}!}$.
nodes.title: Words of given content are counted by the multinomial coefficient

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered alphabet, and order the words over $\alpha$ lexicographically. A word $w$ over $\alpha$ of length $n$ is a Lyndon word if it is nonempty and, for every $k$ with $0 < k < n$, $w$ is strictly smaller than its rotation by $k$, the word obtained by moving the first $k$ letters of $w$ to the end.
nodes.title: Lyndon word

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a word of length $n$, and for $0 \le k < n$ let $w_k$ be the rotation of $w$ by $k$, obtained by moving the first $k$ letters of $w$ to the end. Then $w$ is primitive if and only if $w$ is nonempty and the $n$ words $w_0, w_1, \dots, w_{n-1}$ are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Primitivity via distinct rotations

nodes.summary: Every Lyndon word over a linearly ordered alphabet is primitive.
nodes.title: Lyndon words are primitive

nodes.summary: A nonempty finite word is primitive if it is not a proper power of another word.
nodes.title: Primitive word

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$ and natural numbers $n_0, \dots, n_{r-1}$, the set of Lyndon words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$, ordered as the natural numbers, in which each letter $i$ occurs exactly $n_i$ times.
nodes.title: Lyndon words of given content

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$ and natural numbers $n_0, \dots, n_{r-1}$, the set of primitive words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$ in which each letter $i$ occurs exactly $n_i$ times.
nodes.title: Primitive words of given content

nodes.summary: If $w$ is a primitive word of length $n$ and $0 < k < n$, then the rotation of $w$ by $k$, obtained by moving the first $k$ letters of $w$ to the end, is different from $w$.
nodes.title: Nontrivial rotations move a primitive word

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$ and a word $w$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$, summing over all letters $i$ the number of occurrences of $i$ in $w$ gives the length of $w$.
nodes.title: The content of a word sums to its length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$, words $u$ and $v$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$, and every letter $i$, the number of occurrences of $i$ in the concatenation $uv$ is the number of occurrences of $i$ in $u$ plus the number of occurrences of $i$ in $v$.
nodes.title: Content is additive under concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a word over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$, let $i$ be a letter, and write $c(u)$ for the content of a word $u$ (the number of occurrences of each letter in $u$). If $iw$ denotes $w$ with $i$ prepended, then $c(iw)(i) = c(w)(i) + 1$ and $c(iw)(j) = c(w)(j)$ for every letter $j \ne i$.
nodes.title: Content of a word after prepending a letter

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number. For every letter $i$ of the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$, the content of the one-letter word $i$ takes the value $1$ at $i$ and the value $0$ at every other letter.
nodes.title: Content of a one-letter word

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number. The content of a word $w$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$ is the function that assigns to each letter $i$ the number of occurrences of $i$ in $w$.
nodes.title: Content of a word

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number. Given a function $d$ from the alphabet $\{0, \dots, r-1\}$ to the natural numbers, the words of content $d$ are the words $w$ over this alphabet whose content equals $d$, that is, in which each letter $i$ occurs exactly $d(i)$ times.
nodes.title: Words with prescribed content

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
